newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk refinery 1996 net drops 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk refinery 1996 net drops 35 pct.

text.p: The net profit of the Gdansk refinery dropped by 35 percent in 1996 from 125 million zlotys in 1995, according to preliminary data given by the firm's chief financial officer on Wednesday.
Stanislaw Pokojski told a news conference gross profit fell 42 percent in 1996 from 177 million zlotys in 1995 while sales rose 12 percent to 3.2 billion zlotys.

"The drop in profits is a result of the dramatic, 50 percent jump in world oil prices. The company has been bringing loss for the last three months because it could not raise its prices due to government limits," Pokojski said.
Maximum prices of fuel in Poland are set by the finance ministry, which is reluctant to let them rise because of the fear of inflation.

"We are probably the only European country in which the rise of oil prices does not affect domestic prices. The Gdansk refinery is now subsidising fuel imports," said the refinery's president Wlodzimierz Dyrka, also present.

The Gdansk refinery, Poland's second largest, processed 2.95 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996. It has 14 own petrol stations and 57 franchised filling stations. It plans to build four of its own new stations and franchise 58 new ones.
